newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Dec corn drops to 14-month lows on harvest.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Dec corn drops to 14-month lows on harvest.

text.p: Seasonal harvest pressure and a collapse in soybeans pushed CBOT corn futures to a lower close and nearby December touched a session low of $2.65-1/2 per bushel, a 14-month low, traders said.
The December contract last traded at $2.65-1/2 on September 7, 1995.
"There is good harvest weather for corn and beans," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders said the market shrugged off a bullish USDA weekly export sales report and corn futures declined despite active commercial buying.

USDA Thursday said U.S. corn net sales for the week ended October 24 were 768,900 tonnes, which was above trader expectations, 3-1/2 times more than the previous week and 27 percent above the four-week average.

Chartists said the key moving averages indicate corn remains in a downtrend even though short term indicators showed the market was oversold with December's nine day relative strength index (RSI) closing at 15 points.
Corn closed one to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 4-1/4 at $2.66.
Traders view a market as near oversold status when the RSI falls below 30 points.
December fell below first support at $2.68-1/2 per bushel and was threatened to fall through second support at $2.63-1/2.
Funds and commission houses were the chief sellers of roughly one to two million bushels each, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold six million bushels of December and bought four million December, traders said. Term Commodities bought five million bushels of December, they said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 86,000 contracts, about even with the 86,182 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Smith Barney sold 1,000 May $2.90 calls at nine cents and sold 800 May $3.00 calls at 7-7-1/4 cents, traders said. USA Trading bought 500 May $3.60 calls at one cent, they said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 30,000 contracts, up from 28,560 Wednesday.
